faqHeading: What Baton Rouge asks before renting.

faqs.q: What size do I need?
faqs.a: A bathroom or a single room of flooring usually fits in a 10 or 15 yard. A kitchen, a whole-house flooring job or a big cleanout is a 20. A flooded house or new construction usually needs a 30 or 40. Tell us the job and we will help you pick.

faqs.q: Can it go on the street?
faqs.a: On your own driveway or lot, there is usually nothing to file. If it has to sit on a street or right-of-way in Baton Rouge or one of the surrounding cities, check with that city first.

faqs.q: My yard is soft. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: It can be. A loaded roll-off is heavy, and Baton Rouge ground stays wet a long time after rain. Pick a spot on concrete or a firm drive if you can, and tell us about it when you call.

faqs.q: What can't go in?
faqs.a: Paint, chemicals, oil, tires, batteries and refrigerators or freezers with refrigerant are generally not allowed. Heavy materials like concrete and dirt can go in a box sized for them. Ask if you are unsure.

faqs.q: How long can I keep it?
faqs.a: Rentals are set by days, and you can extend. Call when it is full or when you are done and it gets picked up.

faqs.q: Do you pick up and swap on job sites?
faqs.a: Yes. On construction and big cleanouts, a full box can be hauled and an empty one set down in its place.

sections.body: Live oaks and power lines are the two things that stop a roll-off truck in Baton Rouge. The truck needs to back straight in and tip the box down, so pick a spot with clear room overhead.

sections.heading: Old houses are heavy houses.
sections.body: Older homes in Mid City, the Garden District and Southdowns often have tile set in mortar, plaster walls or layers of old flooring. All of it is heavy. Mention it when you call so the box is sized by weight, not just by space.

sections.heading: Forties for framing, smaller for demo.

sections.heading: Plan for rain, because it is coming.
sections.body: Set the dumpster on the firmest part of the site, and somewhere the truck can still reach after a week of afternoon storms. A rutted access road slows down every swap.

faqs.q: Can appliances go in?

sections.heading: Newer houses, first real remodel.
sections.body: Prairieville does not have an old downtown full of plaster. It has subdivisions, brick fronts, and owners who are finally ripping out the original kitchen or the carpet from 2004. Add a fence that came down, a patio demo, and the pile from a roof. A 20 covers the kitchen and the floor. A 15 covers a bath and a small roof. A 40 is for the new-build sites, not for a cul-de-sac driveway.

sections.heading: Know the days before the truck turns in.
sections.body: The subdivisions off Airline, Highway 73, and Highway 42 almost all have a rule about dumpsters. Some want it on the driveway, not the street. Some want it gone in a set number of days. Read that line, then call us with the number. We will drop the box and pick it up inside the window. The rule is not a reason to haul debris to the dump yourself.

sections.heading: Cul-de-sacs and fresh concrete.
sections.body: A lot of Prairieville drives are wide, which helps, until the box has to sit at the bubble of a cul-de-sac or on a driveway that was poured last month. Tell us. We will keep a loaded roll-off off green concrete and off the edge of the slab. If the only approach is tight, we still deliver in Prairieville. We pick the size that can turn around.

faqs.q: Which size do Prairieville kitchens take?
faqs.a: Most full kitchens are a 20. A bath or a small roof can stay at a 10 or 15.

faqs.q: What about Gonzales?
faqs.a: We drop there too. Different roads, different mix of commercial work. Use that page if the address is Gonzales.

sections.heading: Older houses in town, commercial out on the highways.
sections.body: Near Burnside and the railroad you get remodel debris from older houses: kitchens, floors, a roof after hail. Along Airline, by Tanger, and down Highway 30 the calls are tenant cleanouts, light commercial demo, and construction pads. Highway 44 toward the river is a different driveway again, often longer and sometimes soft. Name the road when you call. We deliver on all of them.

sections.heading: Hail does not care which subdivision it was.
sections.body: When a storm tags Ascension, Gonzales roofs come off in a bunch. Shingles are heavy, so the box is sized by squares and layers, not by how big the house looks from the street. A crew that can throw straight into the box finishes faster. Put the dumpster at the eave, on a spot the truck can still pick up. Book it when the job is sold, not the morning of the tear-off.

sections.heading: A 20 for a house, a 30 or 40 for a site.
sections.body: A rental turnover near Cornerview or in town is usually furniture, carpet, and whatever got left in the shed. That is a 20. A build or a commercial strip wants a 30 or a 40 and a swap when it hits the rail. Keep concrete out of the big box. If you are breaking a slab on Highway 30, say concrete on the call and we will send the small heavy one.

faqs.q: Do you rent roofing dumpsters in Gonzales?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us squares and layers and we will size the box for the weight.

faqs.q: Need more than one box?
faqs.a: Commercial and new builds can run a swap. That is the construction page.

Magnolia Bridge and the low spots near the river are places to say something before we arrive, not after the truck is stuck.

faqs.q: Do you cover Denham Springs from here?

Read the rule, tell us the days, and we will drop it and pick it up on that clock. We deliver in Shenandoah. Have the street address. The subdivision name is not enough. Look up before you pick the spot. If a limb has to be the landmark, describe it. We still put a dumpster on that street.
